title: Places, Devotees & Teachings
about: Shirdi and Dwarkamai, devotees from Hemadpant to Tatya, and teachings like Shraddha and Saburi - the places, people, and values woven around Sai Baba's life. Remembering these names from the Satcharitra strengthens the faith of those who read them.

entries.meaning: The village in Maharashtra where Baba spent his entire life
The ruined mosque where Baba lived; said to be a name he gave it himself
The hall Baba was carried to in procession to rest in every second night
The sacred ash Baba gave devotees as a blessing from his dhuni
The sacred fire Baba kept burning day and night in Dwarkamai
The garden Baba himself planted and watered
The temple deity at whose gate Mhalsapati first called Baba 'Ya Sai'
Where villagers first saw the young Baba meditating under a neem tree
The building a devotee named Buti built, which later became Baba's samadhi mandir
The Khandoba temple priest whose greeting 'Ya Sai' gave Baba his name
Bayajabai's son, a Shirdi villager who spent nearly his whole life close to Baba from childhood
Author of the Satcharitra (real name Govind Raghunath Dabholkar); the name 'Hemadpant' was Baba's own gift to him
One of Baba's closest devotees; Baba said their bond spanned seventy-two lifetimes
Tatya's mother, who served Baba with a mother's love, whom Baba called his sister for seven lifetimes
A Gita scholar, one of Baba's most prominent devotees, a Deputy Collector
A Bombay solicitor who asked Baba to cure 'the lameness of my mind,' not his leg
A devotee who spread Baba's fame through kirtans, at Baba's own urging
A devotee who served Baba with a mother's love and organized the Chavadi procession
The villager whose lost mare Baba found; Baba came to Shirdi with his relative's wedding procession
A devotee who served Baba lifelong despite leprosy; one of only seven present in the mosque at Baba's mahasamadhi
The first of the two qualities Baba taught above all - faith
The second quality Baba taught - patience, perseverance
The bag Baba used to collect alms daily from fixed households
The offering Baba asked some devotees for, then gave away the same day - teaching non-attachment
The sacred guru-worship festival celebrated at Shirdi since 1909
The sacred day Baba left his body - 15 October 1918
The festival begun when Baba's blessing merged it with an Urs started by Gopalrao Gund - a symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity
'God is the Master of all' - a phrase Baba often spoke
The devotee Baba gave nine coins as prasad to, before his mahasamadhi (Lakshmibai Shinde)
A Shiva devotee whose wish to bathe Baba with Ganga water was fulfilled
The Muslim devotee who served Baba daily in Dwarkamai
The prominent devotee (Bapusaheb Jog) who conducted the aartis in Baba's presence
The devotee who avoided a business loss by taking Baba's advice
The Shirdi village officer (Appa Kulkarni) who experienced a leela over dakshina
The educated devotee (Balasaheb Bhate) who grasped the importance of guru-bhakti through Baba
The devotee (Bapusaheb Buti) whose planned Krishna temple became Baba's samadhi mandir instead
The devotee who built a wada for pilgrims near Gurusthan
Shama's real name (Madhavrao Deshpande)
Hemadpant's real name (Govind Raghunath Dabholkar)
The devotee (Kakasaheb Dixit) who built Dixit Wada
A government officer prominent among Baba's devotees, deeply learned in the Gita (Nanasaheb Chandorkar)
The pilgrims' residence built by Kakasaheb Dixit
One of the earliest pilgrim lodgings, built near Gurusthan
The shrine where Baba's sacred body was interred
The garden Baba walked through and meditated in daily
A village near Shirdi that Baba visited now and then
A village near Shirdi that Baba often visited
The nearby town Shirdi pilgrims usually arrive through
The smoking pipe Baba shared and used with devotees
The small stick Baba always kept with him
The long, simple robe Baba wore
The white cloth Baba wrapped around his head
The sacred object Baba rested against during meditation
The prasad Baba gave to Lakshmibai Shinde just before his mahasamadhi
The miracle lamps Baba lit when oil was refused
The grain Baba told devotees to scatter at the village boundary, to ward off cholera
The worship ritual performed daily, in a fixed order, in Baba's presence
The service of Baba himself cooking and feeding everyone
The large pot Baba cooked in himself, for devotees
One of the prasad dishes Baba occasionally made himself in the handi
The daily way of life Baba practiced, as a model for dissolving ego
The main path Baba showed devotees to practice - service
The idea Baba taught of seeing the same divinity in every being
The principle Baba taught as essential to spiritual progress - devotion to the guru
The quality that means steadfastness in spiritual practice
The quality Baba taught of lessening worldly attachment to dwell in divine thought
The virtue Baba taught should be shown to every living being - compassion
The great virtue Baba taught a devotee should cultivate - forgiveness
The epidemic that spread in Shirdi and was warded off by Baba's leela
The sacred tree under which Baba did tapasya in his early days
